category: File types, editions & licensing, version highlights and schematic editor shortcuts
description: Altium Designer document and project file extensions beyond the core .PrjPcb/.SchDoc/.PcbDoc set, product editions, licensing modes, Altium 365 plans and notable features by release, plus the most-used schematic editor keyboard shortcuts.

tools.name: .PrjPcbStructure (project structure file)
tools.description: Companion file created next to a .PrjPcb that records the project's document hierarchy (flat or hierarchical structure, sheet ordering) as computed by the compiler; it is regenerated automatically and should be kept with the project (and in version control) so the Projects panel structure view is consistent.
tools.usage: Auto-generated in the project folder; no manual editing
tools.example: Commit Board.PrjPcb together with Board.PrjPcbStructure; deleting the structure file just triggers regeneration on the next validate.
tools.notes: Harmless to delete; do not confuse with .PrjPcbVariants (variant data, older versions).

tools.name: .BomDoc (ActiveBOM document)
tools.description: The ActiveBOM working document: stores BOM configuration (columns, grouping, line numbers), custom items, chosen solutions/part choices, BOM check settings and supply-chain snapshot. One BomDoc per PCB project; created with Add New to Project > ActiveBOM and consumed by BOM outputs and Draftsman BOM tables.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > ActiveBOM (.BomDoc)
tools.example: Board.BomDoc added to the project; OutJob BOM output set to 'Use BomDoc' so line numbers match the assembly drawing.
tools.notes: Multi-board and harness projects can also carry a BomDoc.

tools.name: .PCBDwf (Draftsman document)
tools.description: Draftsman drawing file linked to a PCB (fabrication/assembly drawings with live views, tables and dimensions). Multi-board projects use .MbDwf and harness projects .HarDwf for their Draftsman documents. Output to PDF/DXF/print through OutJob Documentation Outputs > Draftsman.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Draftsman Document (.PCBDwf / .MbDwf / .HarDwf)
tools.example: Board_Fab.PCBDwf and Board_Assy.PCBDwf in the project, both exported by the release OutJob.
tools.notes: Draftsman templates have their own template extensions managed in Data Management > Templates.

tools.name: .PrjMbd / .MbsDoc / .MbaDoc (multi-board project files)
tools.description: Multi-board design project (.PrjMbd) with its logical Multi-board Schematic (.MbsDoc, modules and connections) and physical Multi-board Assembly (.MbaDoc, placed boards/enclosure with mating and collision data); may also include .BomDoc, .MbDwf and .OutJob documents.
tools.usage: File > New > Project > Multi-board Design Project
tools.example: System.PrjMbd containing System.MbsDoc (three modules) and System.MbaDoc (assembled stack with enclosure STEP).
tools.notes: Child PCB projects are referenced by path; keep them in sibling folders for portability.

tools.name: .PrjHar / .WirDoc / .LdrDoc / .HarDwf (harness project files)
tools.description: Harness design project (.PrjHar) with Harness Wiring Diagram (.WirDoc), Harness Layout Drawing (.LdrDoc), harness Draftsman document (.HarDwf), plus optional .BomDoc and .OutJob. Introduced with Harness Design in Altium Designer 23/24.
tools.usage: File > New > Project > Harness Design Project
tools.example: CableSet.PrjHar with CableSet.WirDoc, CableSet.LdrDoc, CableSet.HarDwf and CableSet.BomDoc.
tools.notes: Distinct from .Harness files, which are schematic signal-harness definitions.

tools.name: .DsnWrk / .PrjGrp (project group / design workspace)
tools.description: Project group file listing several projects opened together (Projects panel root). Historically called Design Workspace (.DsnWrk); newer versions name the concept Project Group (.PrjGrp is the current extension in the File > Save Project Group As dialog, while .DsnWrk files still open). Useful for multi-project systems and shared library packages.
tools.usage: File > Save Project Group As (.PrjGrp / .DsnWrk); File > Open to reopen the group
tools.example: Product.PrjGrp containing MCU.PrjPcb, PSU.PrjPcb, Company.LibPkg and System.PrjMbd.
tools.notes: The group file stores relative project paths; keep it at the top of the folder tree.

tools.name: .LibPkg / .DbLib / .SVNDbLib / .DBLink / .PvLib (library file types)
tools.description: Library-side files: .LibPkg (Integrated Library package project compiling .SchLib/.PcbLib into .IntLib), .DbLib (database library definition), .SVNDbLib (SVN-backed database library), .DBLink (database link for parameter updates without placement), .PvLib (Pad Via Library of pad/via templates). All are installed through Data Management > File-based Libraries or added to a project.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > Integrated Library / Database Library / SVN Database Library / Database Link File / Pad Via Library
tools.example: Company.LibPkg builds Company.IntLib; Parts.DbLib points at the ERP database; Company.PvLib supplies via templates.
tools.notes: .IntLib is read-only; extract sources to edit.

tools.name: .SchDot / .PcbDot (document templates) and .DXPPrf (preferences)
tools.description: Template files: .SchDot (schematic sheet template with border/title block/parameters), .PcbDot (PCB template with layer stack, rules, board shape, mechanical layer setup); Draftsman document/sheet templates are managed via Data Management > Templates. .DXPPrf is the exported Preferences file created by the Preferences dialog's Save button.
tools.usage: File > Save As > choose template type; Preferences > Save/Load (.DXPPrf)
tools.example: Save the configured blank board as Company_6L.PcbDot and set it as the New Document Default for PCB.
tools.notes: Templates may be local or Workspace-managed.

tools.name: .RUL (design rules export), .Cam (CAM document), .sdf (simulation results), .ckt/.mdl (SPICE models)
tools.description: Auxiliary formats: .RUL holds exported PCB design rules (Design > Rules > Export Rules) for reuse; .Cam is the CAMtastic CAM editor document holding imported Gerber/drill layers; .sdf is the SimData waveform/results document produced by the simulator; .ckt (.SUBCKT subcircuits) and .mdl (.MODEL cards) are SPICE model files linked from components' Sim models.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Export/Import Rules (.RUL); File > New > CAM Document (.Cam); Simulation Dashboard results (.sdf); Component Sim model > Model File (.ckt/.mdl)
tools.example: Export Company_4L.RUL from the golden board; import into a new board; open Board.sdf to review simulation results later.
tools.notes: .sdf documents can be added to the project to keep simulation results with the design.

tools.name: Generated output file extensions (Gerber, drill, ODB++, IPC-2581, pick and place)
tools.description: Fabrication outputs use conventional extensions: Gerber .GTL/.GBL (top/bottom copper), .G1..Gn (inner signal), .GP1.. (planes), .GTO/.GBO (overlay), .GTS/.GBS (solder mask), .GTP/.GBP (paste), .GM1.. (mechanical), .GKO (keepout), .GD1/.GG1 (drill drawing/guide), .apr (apertures), .REP (report); Gerber X2 the same with attributes; NC drill .TXT per layer pair plus .DRR (report) and .LDP (layer pairs); ODB++ as a .tgz/.zip folder tree; IPC-2581 .xml/.cvg; pick and place .csv/.txt/.xls; IPC-D-356A .ipc; STEP .step; test point report .txt/.csv.
tools.usage: Generated into Project Outputs by File > Fabrication/Assembly Outputs or an OutJob
tools.example: Zip the Gerber .G* files with Board.TXT/.DRR and the IPC-D-356 netlist for the fabricator; send ODB++ instead when they accept it.
tools.notes: Extensions can be customised in the OutJob's file naming options (Use custom file names).

tools.name: Altium Designer editions and licensing (On-demand, Standalone, Private Server)
tools.description: Licences are subscription-based per seat (Altium Designer with Altium 365 subscription, or the higher Altium Designer Pro/Enterprise bundles) and served in three modes: On-Demand (floating, checked out from the Altium licensing service via account sign-in, roaming supported), Standalone (a licence file bound to one machine, for offline use) and Private Server (a licence server on the company network for shared floating seats). Licence management is under the Home > Licenses page inside Altium Designer.
tools.usage: Altium Designer Home page > Licenses (Sign in, Use, Roam, Add standalone license file, Setup private license server)
tools.example: Sign in, select the On-Demand licence, click Use; before travelling click Roam for 30 days offline use.
tools.notes: Feature availability (e.g. Harness Design, multi-board, Constraint Manager) can depend on the subscription tier.

tools.name: Altium 365 Workspace plans (Standard, Pro, Enterprise) and Altium Enterprise Server
tools.description: Altium 365 is the cloud platform bundled with the subscription: a Workspace provides managed components, project version control, sharing/comments, web viewer, manufacturing packages and release management; Pro and Enterprise tiers add folder-level access control, requirements/PLM integration, advanced BOM/supply chain (e.g. Component Intelligence), simulation cloud, and ERP connectors. Altium Enterprise Server (formerly Concord Pro / NEXUS Server) is the on-premises equivalent for organisations that cannot use the cloud; Altium Designer connects to either through Preferences > Data Management > Servers.
tools.usage: Altium Designer Home page > Workspaces (create/join); Preferences > Data Management > Servers
tools.example: Team joins the company Workspace; projects are created with 'Save to Workspace' so history, comments and releases are centralised.
tools.notes: Naming has changed over the years (Vault > Concord Pro > Enterprise Server); documentation for each is under altium.com/documentation.

tools.name: Altium Designer Viewer (free viewer) and view-only mode
tools.description: Altium Designer Viewer is a free, read-only installation that opens Altium projects and documents (schematics, PCBs, Draftsman, BOM) for review, measurement and printing without a full licence; separately, the full product can be launched in a View-Only mode (System.ViewOnlyMode.Support) and Altium 365's web viewer offers browser-based viewing without any install.
tools.usage: Download Altium Designer Viewer from altium.com; or share the project via Altium 365 web viewer
tools.example: Send a mechanical engineer the Altium 365 share link instead of exporting PDFs; they inspect layers and measure in the browser.
tools.notes: The viewer cannot edit or generate outputs.

tools.name: CircuitStudio and CircuitMaker versus Altium Designer
tools.description: CircuitStudio was Altium's mid-range paid product sharing the AD file formats with a reduced feature set (no multi-board, limited scripting/rules, no Draftsman) and is discontinued; CircuitMaker is the free community edition (cloud-hosted projects, community libraries, limited to non-commercial use, simplified UI, .PcbDoc/.SchDoc compatible). Both open in Altium Designer, but AD projects using advanced features may not open fully in them.
tools.usage: Reference only; open CircuitMaker/CircuitStudio files directly in Altium Designer
tools.example: A CircuitMaker hobby project migrated to Altium Designer: add design rules, Draftsman and OutJobs that CircuitMaker lacked.
tools.notes: Upstream is the free web-based schematic/PCB tool; Altium 365 Viewer is free for viewing.

tools.name: Altium Designer version highlights (22-25)
tools.description: Notable additions by release: AD22 - Constraints Editor preview, improved Layer Stack Manager and PDF3D; AD23 - Harness Design (beta), multi-board improvements, Simulation Dashboard refinements; AD24 - Constraint Manager (unified constraints from schematic and PCB), Harness Design generally available, glossing/routing engine updates, Design Comments and Altium 365 requirements; AD25 - Constraint Manager extensions, enhanced interactive routing and 3D, updated Components panel/Manufacturer Part Search and cloud simulation options. Check the 'New in Altium Designer' page for the exact per-version list.
tools.usage: Help > About shows version; altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/new lists per-release features
tools.example: Projects created in AD24 with Constraint Manager cannot revert to the rules editor in AD22; keep team versions aligned.
tools.notes: File formats are generally forward-compatible; older versions warn when opening newer documents.

tools.name: Schematic: Space / Shift+Space / X / Y (rotate and mirror while placing or moving)
tools.description: While a part, port, net label or other object is being placed or moved: Space rotates 90 degrees counter-clockwise, Shift+Space rotates clockwise, X mirrors about the X axis (flip vertically), Y mirrors about the Y axis (flip horizontally). During wire/bus placement Space toggles the corner start/end sub-mode and Shift+Space cycles placement modes (90 Degree, 45 Degree, Any Angle, Auto Wire).
tools.usage: Space | Shift+Space | X | Y (object floating on the cursor)
tools.example: Place > Part, choose a resistor, press Space to make it vertical and X to flip pin order, click to place.
tools.notes: Mirroring symbols can confuse readers; prefer rotation for polarised parts.

tools.name: Schematic: Tab and Insert while placing
tools.description: Tab opens the Properties panel for the object being placed (designator, comment, footprint, net label text, port name/I-O type) and the values persist for subsequent placements with auto-increment; Insert, while placing, copies attributes from the object under the cursor (or adds a vertex during wire placement).
tools.usage: Tab | Insert (during placement)
tools.example: Place > Net Label, Tab, type D0, place: subsequent labels auto-increment D1, D2...
tools.notes: Auto-increment step is set in Preferences > Schematic > General.

tools.name: Schematic: wire placement keys (Shift+Space, Space, Backspace, Ctrl+Space, Esc)
tools.description: During Place > Wire/Bus/Harness: Shift+Space cycles modes 90 Degree / 45 Degree / Any Angle / Auto Wire (auto-routes around obstacles), Space toggles which corner bends first, Backspace removes the last vertex, Ctrl+Space changes the wiring mode of connected wires, clicking on a pin or wire end terminates the wire at that point, Esc or right-click ends the wire, Enter commits.
tools.usage: P W then Shift+Space | Space | Backspace | Ctrl+Space | Esc
tools.example: P W, click pin 1, press Shift+Space until Auto Wire, click the destination pin: the wire routes around the IC.
tools.notes: Wires ending on a pin's hotspot auto-connect; check the Connective Insight graph to verify.

tools.name: Schematic: placement accelerators (P P, P W, P B, P U, P N, P R, P O, P S, P E, P T, P H)
tools.description: Menu accelerator sequences of the Place menu: P P Part, P W Wire, P B Bus, P U Bus Entry, P N Net Label, P R Port, P O Power Port, P S Sheet Symbol, P E (Add) Sheet Entry, P T Text String, P F Text Frame, P H Harness sub-menu, P J Junction (manual), plus the Directives and Drawing Tools sub-menus. Letters follow the underlined menu mnemonics and can be verified in the menu.
tools.usage: Press P then the underlined letter of the Place menu item (e.g. P W)
tools.example: P N, Tab, type CLK, click to place; P O for a GND power port, Tab to set style Power Ground.
tools.notes: Mnemonics may differ by localisation; the menu shows the underlined letters.

tools.name: Schematic: view shortcuts (PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl+PgDn, Home, End, V F, V D)
tools.description: PgUp/PgDn zoom in/out around the cursor, Ctrl+PgDn fits all objects (View > Fit All Objects), V D fits the document sheet, V F fits all objects, V A zooms to an area, Home centres the view on the cursor, End redraws, Ctrl+Wheel zooms, Ctrl+M measures a distance; Alt+Click on a net highlights it across sheets (Navigation preference).
tools.usage: PgUp | PgDn | Ctrl+PgDn | Home | End | V D | V F | V A | Ctrl+M
tools.example: Ctrl+PgDn to see the whole sheet, V A to drag a zoom box around the MCU.
tools.notes: Mouse wheel behaviour is configurable in System > Mouse Wheel Configuration.

tools.name: Schematic: selection and find (Ctrl+A, Shift+Click, X A, Shift+F, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, J C)
tools.description: Ctrl+A selects all, Shift+Click toggles an object's selection, the Edit > Select sub-menu (Inside Area, Outside Area, Touching Line/Rectangle, Lasso, All, Connection, Net) and Edit > Deselect > All (X A) manage selections, Shift+F starts Find Similar Objects, Ctrl+F opens Find Text (F3 finds next), Ctrl+H Find and Replace Text, J C jumps to a component by designator, and the Navigator panel or Alt+Click locate nets. Selection memories Ctrl+1..8 store/recall selections.
tools.usage: Ctrl+A | Shift+Click | X A | Shift+F | Ctrl+F | Ctrl+H | J C | Ctrl+1..8
tools.example: Shift+F on a resistor, set Comment = Same, Apply: all 10k resistors are selected for a bulk Properties edit.
tools.notes: Selection memory shortcuts are shown in Edit > Selection Memory.

tools.name: Schematic: editing shortcuts (Ctrl+drag, Ctrl+X/C/V, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+D, E W, Delete, Ctrl+Z)
tools.description: Ctrl+drag moves a part without its wires when Always Drag is on (or drags with wires when off), Ctrl+C/X/V copy/cut/paste (Ctrl+V pastes relative to the reference point chosen on copy), Ctrl+R Rubber Stamp (copy and immediately place repeatedly), Ctrl+D Duplicate, E W Break Wire, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y undo/redo, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+Shift+V Smart Paste.
tools.usage: Ctrl+drag | Ctrl+C | Ctrl+V | Ctrl+R | Ctrl+Shift+V | E W | Delete | Ctrl+Z
tools.example: Select a decoupling capacitor with its power labels, Ctrl+R, click five times to stamp five copies with incremented designators.
tools.notes: Smart Paste converts clipboard net labels to ports and other object conversions.

tools.name: Schematic: menu accelerators for validate, ECO and tools (D U, D I, T A Q, T G, C O)
tools.description: Frequently used menu accelerator sequences (press the underlined letters): Design > Update PCB Document (D U), Design > Import Changes From PCB (D I), Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics Quietly (T A Q), Tools > Footprint Manager (T G), Project > Project Options (C O), Reports > Bill of Materials (R I), and Project > Validate PCB Project from the Project (C) menu. Mnemonics follow the underlined letters of the current menu layout.
tools.usage: C then the menu letter (Project menu); D U (Update PCB); T A Q (annotate quietly)
tools.example: T A Q, then Project > Validate PCB Project, then D U to push the ECO to the PCB.
tools.notes: Confirm letters in your build by opening the menu with Alt; they occasionally change between releases.

tools.name: Schematic: Ctrl+Space (re-route attached wires) and Alt+Click (net highlight)
tools.description: Ctrl+Space, while dragging a wire end or component, cycles how attached wires are re-routed (keep 90 degrees, 45 degrees, any angle); Alt+Click on a wire or net label selects the whole net and highlights it project-wide using the Navigation preferences; the Navigator panel offers the same net browsing with zoom.
tools.usage: Ctrl+Space (while dragging); Alt+Click (net highlight); Shift+C clears highlight
tools.example: Alt+Click the SCL wire to see every sheet where SCL is used; Shift+C to clear.
tools.notes: Net highlight colour is configurable in Preferences > Schematic > Graphical Editing > Color Options.

tools.name: Global shortcuts (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+F4, F1, F9, Ctrl+S, Alt+F4)
tools.description: Environment-wide keys: Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch documents, Ctrl+F4 closes the document, F1 opens context help for the object/keyword/dialog under the cursor, F9 runs the current script (script editor), Ctrl+S saves, Alt+F4 exits; panels are opened from View > Panels or the Panels button at the bottom-right of the window and have no default hotkeys.
tools.usage: Ctrl+Tab | Ctrl+F4 | F1 | F9 | Ctrl+S
tools.example: Hover over 'InNetClass' in a rule scope and press F1 to open the keyword reference.
tools.notes: Custom shortcuts are assigned per command in the Customizing Editor (right-click a menu > Customize).

tools.name: Customize (assign keyboard shortcuts and menu items)
tools.description: The Customizing Editor (right-click the menu bar > Customize, or DXP > Customize) lists every command by category with its process (e.g. PCB:Zoom), parameters, caption, shortcut and alternative shortcut; commands can be dragged onto menus/toolbars and given key combinations, and new commands can be created that run processes or scripts (ScriptingSystem:RunScript). This is also how scripts get toolbar buttons and hotkeys.
tools.usage: Right-click menu bar > Customize > Commands tab > select command > Edit shortcut; New to create a command with Process and Parameters

parameters.name: Process / Parameters
parameters.description: Server:Command string and parameter string for a new command.

tools.example: New command: Process ScriptingSystem:RunScript, Parameters ProjectName=D:\Scripts\Tools.PrjScr|ProcName=Tools.pas>Cleanup, shortcut Ctrl+Alt+K, drag it onto the Tools menu.
tools.notes: Customisations are stored per editor (PCB, Sch...) in the user profile; export via Preferences Save.

tools.name: Panels menu shortcuts and panel management
tools.description: Panels are opened from View > Panels or the Panels button (bottom-right); frequently used panels can be pinned, docked, floated or grouped in tabs; the Properties panel is context-sensitive (double-click objects); no panel hotkeys exist by default beyond those assigned via Customize. View > Desktop Layouts saves/loads panel arrangements.
tools.usage: View > Panels > <panel>; Panels button; View > Desktop Layouts > Save / Load
tools.example: Dock PCB, Properties and PCB Filter on the right, Projects/Navigator left, save as 'Layout' desktop layout.
tools.notes: Panels remember state per document kind.
